sample_unit: published case reports (1792 manually assigned HPO terms)

links.outcome: Rate of hallucinated HPO terms among false positives from retrieval-augmented LLM output
links.effect: Of 1648 returned terms, 315 (19.1%) were false positives; only 1/315 (<1%) was a hallucination, 4/315 (1.3%) unrelated, and 300/315 (95.2%) broader ancestor terms.
links.quote: Among these, < 1% (1/315) represented hallucinations, and 1.3% (4/315) represented terms with no ontological relationship to the desired target; the remaining false positives (95.2%, 300/315) were broader ancestor terms of the target term, which may still be relevant to users in many contexts.

unlisted_practices: Retrieval-augmented generation with a vector database of HPO phrases to improve LLM phenotype term assignment without fine-tuning

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks RAG-HPO, evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) added to an LLM to mitigate hallucinations and ground phenotypic extraction from clinical text against standard benchmarks.
